clue.text: Tchaikovsky hero's individual spirit

parts.note: a single individual is one
gin is a distilled spirit

explanation.surface: A remark on the solitary, independent temperament of the leading man in a Tchaikovsky opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' seems to mean character or temperament; here it is a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Eugene Onegin is the title character of Tchaikovsky's opera after Pushkin's verse novel.

clue.text: Traction's treatment for druggy

definitions.note: an adjective-like noun use: one who takes narcotics

indicators.note: a treatment works over and processes material, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: the word with its possessive S, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A hospital patient in traction is given drugs as part of the care.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive S counts as a letter of the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A narcotist is someone addicted to or using narcotics, which is what a druggy person is.

clue.text: Composer's connection between notes

indicators.note: something placed between two things sits inside them, flanked on each side

parts.note: two musical notes, G and A, flanking the insert
a link is a connection

explanation.surface: A musician's notation linking notes, like a slur or tie.
explanation.definitionFit: Mikhail Glinka was a Russian composer, often called the father of Russian classical music.

clue.text: Winkle with sodium compared with iodine on top of …

parts.note: Na is the chemical symbol for sodium
'than' is the word used when comparing
I is the chemical symbol for iodine
the dots carry on into 5-down, whose wordplay opens with 'a line', an elevated railway or el

explanation.surface: A chemistry-sounding recipe pairing a shellfish with elements, trailing off mid-thought.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'on top of' puts iodine above what follows; the ellipsis sends you to the next clue for that, 'a line', the American el or elevated railway.
explanation.definitionFit: Nathaniel Winkle is one of Mr Pickwick's companions in Dickens's Pickwick Papers, so his first name answers to his surname.

clue.text: Call, in poet's translation, for one with jewelled ear

indicators.note: one item goes inside the other
translating turns words into another form, so these letters are rendered in a new order

parts.note: the poet's word, its letters to be rearranged
hi is a call of greeting

explanation.surface: A literary note on how a poet's phrase about a bejewelled ear should be rendered in translation.
explanation.walkthrough: Romeo says Juliet hangs on the cheek of night 'like a rich jewel in an Ethiop's ear'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethiop is the old poetic word for an Ethiopian, and Shakespeare's famous simile gives one a jewel in the ear.

clue.text: Spanish hero with a line to the Yard?

parts.note: an el is an elevated railway line in American usage
the Criminal Investigation Department of Scotland Yard

explanation.surface: A Spanish champion seems to have a direct line to Scotland Yard, London's police headquarters.
explanation.walkthrough: Scotland Yard is the London Metropolitan Police headquarters; its CID is the detective branch.
explanation.definitionFit: El Cid, Rodrigo Díaz de Vivar, is the medieval Castilian warrior celebrated as Spain's national hero.

clue.text: Goldie embracing the Thunderer for the first part of 26

indicators.note: to embrace is to wrap one's arms round, so one name holds the other inside

parts.note: the actress Goldie Hawn
the Norse god of thunder

explanation.surface: A Hollywood actress hugging a thundering god, all on behalf of some other clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 26 is MAYHEM, whose first part is MAY, a country name for hawthorn blossom.
explanation.definitionFit: May is the common name for the hawthorn shrub and its blossom, which flowers in that month.

clue.text: Going into the red compared with 17?

indicators.note: going into a phrase means looking inside its words for a run of letters

parts.note: the letters straddle the three words, starting at the end of the first

explanation.surface: Slipping into debt, set against being in credit.
explanation.walkthrough: 17 is IN THE BLACK; being in the red is the alternative state to that, which makes the definition fair as well as the hiding place apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Set beside being in credit, debt is the contrasting state, the alternative of the pair.

clue.text: Said solver's treated amorously, not like Burns's love

indicators.note: said tells us to go by what is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: the solver is you, so this is your being kissed

explanation.surface: Someone tells the solver they have been romanced, though not the Burns way.
explanation.walkthrough: Burns wrote 'my love is like a red, red rose'; a Yorkist wore the white rose of York in the Wars of the Roses.
explanation.definitionFit: Yorkists took the white rose as their badge, so unlike Burns's red rose.

clue.text: Small objects during the last programme with 21 6, they say

indicators.note: something happening during a period falls within it

parts.note: yester means last or previous, as in yesterday
minis are small things, such as small cars or skirts

explanation.surface: A puzzle about small items in a final broadcast with a named star.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 6 reads NIGEL HAWTHORN; the actor Nigel Hawthorne, spelt with an E, played Sir Humphrey, hence 'they say'.
explanation.definitionFit: The BBC sitcom about a government minister and his civil servant starred Sir Nigel Hawthorne as Sir Humphrey Appleby.

clue.text: Put the frighteners on abandoned byre

parts.note: to cow is to intimidate
shed means cast off or discarded

explanation.surface: Someone intimidated into staying away from a derelict farm building.
explanation.definitionFit: A byre is the farm building where cattle are housed, a shed for cows.

clue.text: Author of computing system, a plaything for even half a TV outfit

parts.note: DOS, disk operating system
a toy is a plaything

indicators.note: half of a word means only part of its letters, here its front

parts.note: the first two of its four letters
Sky is a British satellite television company

explanation.surface: A writer of software is building a toy for a television company.
explanation.walkthrough: Sky is a British pay-TV broadcaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Fyodor Dostoyevsky was the Russian novelist who wrote Crime and Punishment.

clue.text: The usual runs on banks from investments

parts.note: stock means usual or standard, as in a stock answer
sandbanks, or sands, are banks in the sea
to hare is to run fast

explanation.surface: Investments are where the familiar panicky runs on banks come from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runs on banks' looks like a financial panic; in an across clue 'on' puts the runs after the banks.
explanation.definitionFit: Stocks and shares are the standard securities bought and held as financial investments.

clue.text: In which pupil appears to flag

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the coloured ring of the eye, with the pupil at its centre
second meaning: the yellow flag, a wild plant of that genus

explanation.surface: A schoolchild seems to be coming forward to signal or to tire.
explanation.walkthrough: The pupil is the eye's, not a schoolchild; flag is the plant, not a banner or a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The pupil sits in the centre of the eye's coloured ring, and flags are plants of that genus.

clue.text: Painter given money to turn fish-eater

parts.note: tin is old slang for money
taken as written

indicators.note: turning something round makes it face the other way, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: the otter eats fish

explanation.surface: An artist offered cash to take up a diet of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Tintoretto was a Venetian Renaissance painter of the sixteenth century.

clue.text: What the spy in the cab said about cat, pig and sheep

definitions.text: What the spy in the cab said

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word that follows faces back

parts.note: taken as written
a hog is a pig
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: An undercover agent in a taxi gossips about a farmyard of animals.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'spy in the cab' is the tachograph, the device in a lorry cab recording speed and driving hours.
explanation.definitionFit: A tachogram is the record produced by a tachograph, the monitoring device fitted in lorry cabs.

clue.text: A lake you have drunk — reel with mirth

indicators.note: a drunk person staggers about, so the letters lurch into a new order

parts.note: the letters of these words, 'with' just joining them

explanation.surface: Someone tipsy staggers about laughing beside a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' joins the two fodder words and supplies no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Thirlmere is a reservoir lake in the English Lake District, supplying water to Manchester.

clue.text: Factor caused by mirth arising during meals?

definitions.note: the answer is the word that goes with 'factor' in the set phrase

indicators.note: something happening during a period falls within its span

parts.note: meals are food, here split round the insert

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means the letters read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: glee is merriment

explanation.surface: Laughter breaking out round the dinner table is what makes people feel good.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed key's FEELCOLD is a misprint: the wordplay plainly builds FEEL-GOOD, and both differing letters are unchecked. 'Factor' defines it via the phrase feel-good factor.
explanation.definitionFit: The feel-good factor is the stock phrase for a general sense of optimism and wellbeing, so the answer completes it.

clue.text: Not owing a pound, retired into fitted kitchen

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing backwards, so the letters go back to front
one part is placed inside the other
a fitted kitchen has been built to a new layout, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: its letters to be rearranged
A as written plus LB, the abbreviation for a pound in weight

explanation.surface: A pensioner, debt-free, puts money into a new built-in kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in credit, with a positive balance, is the opposite of owing money.

clue.text: Elemental spirit?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: two of the four classical elements side by side

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a sprite or nature spirit; the two classical elements together give a slang name for strong drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Firewater is slang for strong liquor, and the two halves are classical elements alongside earth and air.

clue.text: Initially short and fat from Australian beer

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: the first letter of the word
tubby means plump

explanation.surface: A stocky physique blamed on drinking Australian beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short and fat' reads as one description, but 'and' only joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australia a stubby is a small squat bottle of beer.

clue.text: Fish getting mad among non-alcoholic drinks by 4 6, they say

indicators.note: to be among things is to be in their midst

parts.note: TT, teetotal, plus ales
to angle is to fish
wood is an archaic word for mad

explanation.surface: An angler going crazy in a temperance bar, by some numbered person.
explanation.walkthrough: 4 6 is NATHANIEL HAWTHORN, spelt as the author Nathaniel Hawthorne sounds, hence 'they say'. TT means teetotal.
explanation.definitionFit: Tanglewood Tales is Nathaniel Hawthorne's book of Greek myths retold for children.

clue.text: Boy goes on batting when uplifted

indicators.note: in a down entry, lifting up reads the letters from the bottom

parts.note: in cricket the on side is also called the leg side
a batsman at the crease is in

explanation.surface: A lad keeps batting while lifted in the air.
explanation.walkthrough: The on side in cricket is the half of the field behind the batsman's legs, called the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: Nigel is a boy's first name, and crosswords often use boy for any male name.

clue.text: See 18
Poisonous yellow deformed stunted growth, after the Sun

indicators.note: after says the reworked growth comes second, following the god's name

parts.note: Ra is the Egyptian sun god

indicators.note: something deformed is misshapen, so the letters are twisted out of order
something stunted is cut short, so the word loses its tail

parts.note: taken as written before its last letter goes

explanation.surface: A toxic yellow plant twisted and stunted by sunlight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After the Sun' places the shortened, rearranged word after the god's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragwort is a yellow-flowered weed that is poisonous to grazing horses and cattle.

clue.text: Abstraction to go with daylight

definitions.meaning: first meaning: removal or taking away, a formal word for theft
second meaning: the word completing a set phrase for blatant overcharging

explanation.surface: An artist's idea of abstract art suited to natural light.
explanation.walkthrough: Abstraction looks like an art term; in law it means taking something unlawfully.
explanation.definitionFit: Theft is legally called abstraction, as with electricity, and daylight robbery is the idiom for outrageous overcharging.

clue.text: Italian and German articles in silent flight

definitions.note: describes the craft rather than naming it

parts.note: gli is a plural Italian definite article
der is a German definite article

explanation.surface: Grammar notes on foreign definite articles, oddly airborne and silent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Articles' serves both languages: GLI and DER both mean 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: A glider is an unpowered aircraft that flies without engine noise.

clue.text: A month on the border produces chaos

parts.note: May is a month
a hem is the border of a cloth

explanation.surface: A month of trouble at a frontier leads to disorder.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayhem is violent disorder or confusion, a synonym of chaos.
